title.narrative: NIHR RIGHT - Co-creation of a national technology-enabled program to support weight management in Thailand

description.narrative:
This project aims to support the prevention of cardiovascular disease in Thailand by developing, testing, and preparing for scale-up a national, technology-enabled weight management programme within the primary healthcare system. Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in Thailand, and overweight and obesity are major contributors to this burden, particularly among older adults, low-income groups, and people living in rural or remote areas.
Working closely with the Thai Ministry of Public Health, healthcare providers, and community members, the project will first analyse behavioural, technological, and organisational factors that influence weight management and use of digital health tools. Using these findings, the team will co-create two versions of a technology-enabled weight management programme at different cost levels, designed to be accessible and acceptable to diverse population groups, including those who are digitally underserved.
The project will then evaluate the effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and equity of these interventions through a large cluster randomised trial involving approximately 4,500 adults across 60 primary healthcare centres in two regions of Thailand. Outcomes will include changes in body weight and cardiovascular risk, as well as programme uptake and implementation feasibility. The findings will be used to develop service standards to support national rollout in Thailand and to inform similar initiatives in neighbouring countries, including Laos and Cambodia.
